minutes.headline: Town meeting passed the FY26 school and town budget with deep staff cuts and voted on a $948,000 school override.
minutes.summary: Annual Town Meeting worked through the full warrant: consent-calendar articles, a Wetlands revolving fund, prior-year bills, reserve-fund transfers, a contested capital plan, the $44M-plus Omnibus budget (which includes deep school staffing cuts as one-time ESSER and ARPA funds expire), a $948,000 Proposition 2½ override for the schools that still needs town-election approval, salary and leave-policy changes for non-union employees, the sewer enterprise budget, a cemetery-lots appropriation, a lowered senior property-tax exemption age, re-adoption of the OPEB trust statute, a historical commission bylaw codification, and a new battery-storage/solar zoning bylaw. Numerous floor amendments were proposed on the capital plan, the cemetery appropriation, and the parental-leave article, with mixed results, and the override's final town-meeting vote tally was not clearly announced in the captions.

decisions.decision: Moderator declared a quorum present (50 required) and the meeting properly warranted, then opened the meeting.
Moderator deferred a follow-up question about whether teachers would be cut regardless of the override until Article 8 was reached.
School committee members stated they intend, though are not formally obligated, to return the ARPA-funded operating items to the select board for reappropriation if the override passes.
Personnel committee agreed the idea of a formal sick-time donation bank for SAP employees needs further work and should be considered in a future cycle rather than in this amendment.
Board of Assessors indicated it plans to review and possibly lower income/asset eligibility limits for the senior tax exemption in the fall.
Meeting concluded informally without a formal adjournment motion once the warrant's articles were exhausted.

what_happened.line: Town meeting approved the town/school Omnibus budget 309-37, which includes deep school staffing cuts as one-time COVID relief funds run out.
Town meeting also acted on a Proposition 2½ override for the schools, an amount heard as roughly an amount as heard but the final tally was not clearly announced in the recording.
The override still needs separate approval at a town election before it can take effect.
The FY25 capital plan passed 320-31 after floor amendments to cut Turkey Hill safety-film and Wallace Park court funding both failed.
Town meeting changed the parental sick-leave policy for non-union employees, passing it as amended 123-13.

why_it_matters: The Omnibus budget sets what schools and town departments can spend this year, and the staffing cuts tied to it follow the expiration of temporary federal pandemic aid, not a new decision to cut on its own.
The override next goes to a town-election ballot; if approved there, it would raise the tax levy above the state's normal cap specifically to fund schools.
The capital plan funds building and site work, including two disputed projects, at Turkey Hill and Wallace Park, that residents will see this year.
